findings.message: The 092 AC-5 'In Prod' fix only reaches the ProjectPage card (`releasedLabel`). The Proposals list makes the same claim in two more places and those still use the old rule (`phase === "released"` ⇒ Prod). The 'Shipped to' cell (line 149) shows a green `Prod` chip, and the CSV export (line 122) writes `Prod` in 'Shipped to'. Both should read `releasedLabel(p)` / `p.inProd`, so all three places share one rule. Add list and CSV rows to the board-092 variant table.
findings.scenario: A history change brought in from the repo's archive (CON-801: source 'specclaw', no release) or a release whose Prod deployment was voided → the project board says 'Released · from repo' / 'Released', but /proposals/released shows 'Shipped to: Prod' and proposals.csv writes 'Prod' for the same proposal.

findings.message: The new Owner-line regex lets `'`, `*`, `_`, `{`, `|` and similar characters start the captured local part, but its boundary set `[\s<(\[`":]` doesn't contain them. So any markup or quote placed before the address becomes part of the captured email. The old regex excluded `'`, so a single-quoted owner worked before and breaks now. The same defect is copied to plugins/amax/scripts/read-specclaw.mjs:69. Fix: add `'` (and `*`, `_`) to the boundary class and stop the local part from starting or ending with them. Add those cases to the owner-092 AC-2 table.
findings.scenario: `**Owner:** 'nimal@lumenlabs.test'` → owner `'nimal@lumenlabs.test` (before this diff: `nimal@lumenlabs.test`). ownerFromRepo finds nobody, and because the email isn't undefined the sync overwrites the stored owner with null. Likewise `**Owner:** _nimal@lumenlabs.test_` → `_nimal@lumenlabs.test`.

findings.message: createProposal claims its agent-first check is 'checked under the project lock a sync also takes, so a first sync landing meanwhile is seen'. No test runs a real first sync against a concurrent manual create. agent-first-093.test.ts plants the synced row by hand and then calls createProposal in a single session, so it stays green if the `for update` lock (or the ordering of the check after it) is deleted. Add a two-transaction test: one transaction holds the project lock mid-sync while createProposal for the same project waits, and the create is refused once the sync commits.
findings.scenario: Delete `select 1 from delivery.project ... for update` or move `agentFirstRepo` above it → every 093 test still passes, though a create racing the first sync could add a hand-made proposal to a project that has just become agent-first.

findings.message: The rule counts any specclaw-source proposal in the project, including ones written by sync_proposal or the self-sync before any repo was linked, and withdrawn ones. So linking a repo to a project that already has synced rows makes it agent-first at once, before that repo has synced anything. The README says "a freshly linked project keeps manual creation until its first sync". Either tie the rule to rows synced since the current link (e.g. sync_push for repo_url), or correct the README.
findings.scenario: FLT has a specclaw row from an earlier sync_proposal call and no repo. linkProjectRepo(FLT) → agentFirst=true immediately, and New proposal disappears though the linked repo has never synced.
